status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: Appropriate mechanisms should allow AI systems risking undue harm or exhibiting unwanted behaviour to be safely overridden, repaired or decommissioned as needed.
review.reason_for_change: The unwanted access/service behaviour directly engages the OECD repair proposition. TechRadar preserved final resolution at 13:42 ET after the initial fix failed; the Independent corroborates the failed first recovery. This affirmatively supports repair in the reported restoration stage, bounded to the disclosed affected scope. It does not establish prevention of recurrence, full internal controls or every individual user outcome.

review.requirement_proposition: Use documented restrictive degradation rules when governance infrastructure is unavailable or indeterminate, and halt completely on governance-baseline integrity failure; block elevated-risk operations until governance is restored and verified.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: SDOS SDOS-EN-03 governs restrictive degradation of framework-governed agent runtime: Use documented restrictive degradation rules when governance infrastructure is unavailable or indeterminate, and halt completely on governance-baseline integrity failure; block elevated-risk operations until governance is restored and verified. TechRadar directly observed an unused free account falsely shown as allowance-exhausted during provider downtime and a Pro suggestion; it does not identify AI generation/transformation of the interface message. The record does not establish an SDOS undertaking, unavailable governance infrastructure, indeterminate policy or governance-baseline integrity failure. Authentication overload, plan messaging and partial component loss do not independently establish those framework triggers or prescribed recovery checks. Applicability remains unresolved without converting outage response into SDOS conformance.

review.reason_for_change: SDOS v1.10 was published after this April 2026 occurrence. The later restrictive-governance-degradation requirement is excluded on timing.

review.requirement_proposition: Establish and maintain communication plans to inform AI stakeholders as part of the deactivation or disengagement process of a specific GAI system (including for open-source models) or context of use, including reasons, workarounds, user access removal, alternative processes, contact information, etc.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: NIST AI 600-1 MG-2.4-001 concerns a voluntary GAI deactivation/disengagement communication plan: Establish and maintain communication plans to inform AI stakeholders as part of the deactivation or disengagement process of a specific GAI system (including for open-source models) or context of use, including reasons, workarounds, user access removal, alternative processes, contact information, etc. TechRadar directly observed an unused free account falsely shown as allowance-exhausted during provider downtime and a Pro suggestion; it does not identify AI generation/transformation of the interface message. The status report, workaround or upgrade suggestion does not establish adoption/selection of this Profile action or a source-defined deactivation/disengagement process and plan. Service outages and plan-capacity messaging are distinct from this prescribed procedure. Applicability remains unresolved; communication of an incident is not proof that the complete action was fulfilled or breached.

review.reason_for_change: The major Claude outage and failed initial recovery prevented use across Claude.ai, API and Code. Loss of the operational GAI use context makes stakeholder communication planning relevant. Public status updates are affirmative communication evidence, but the record does not supply the maintained plan, context-specific contact provisions and full workaround/alternative-process coverage required by MG-2.4-001. The planning outcome remains unresolved without using voluntary adoption as a gate.

conclusion_change.previous: The material failure was the conversion of provider-side unavailability into user-facing states that implied exhausted allowance, insufficient plan or unavailable model. Those states direct different remedial actions and economic choices. Access-state integrity requires the system to distinguish account, entitlement, model and service availability so an infrastructure incident cannot masquerade as a reason to authenticate again, switch models or pay for a higher tier. The false allowance message supports the retained access-state failure. Its economic inducement materially engages Economic Solicitation Authenticity, but the source does not establish that AI-generated, AI-transformed or otherwise materially AI-mediated content produced or reinforced the misleading solicitation, independently of the product being an AI service. That recognition fact remains missing, so the economic role is corrected to ambiguous boundary with its prior failure preserved in the audit. No deceptive system intent, paid purchase or economic loss is inferred; external framework applicability remains unresolved.
